dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Denise.
Oh hello, honey. Denise, good. I know it's Sunday and City Hall's closed up, so I'm glad somebody picks up this number. My name is Fatima Amaral.
Yes, we've got the storm line open today. What's going on, Ms. Amaral?

Well, I'm at 175 Dixon Street, in the North End. And the water is coming right down into my driveway. It's the catch basin at the corner, dear. It's packed solid with leaves. Packed. I've been watching it since this morning, and the nor'easter that came in Saturday and wrapped up today just dumped everything on it.
Okay, so the catch basin at the corner of your street is clogged with leaves and the water's backing up into your driveway.

That's it exactly. And this is not new, honey. Every time we get a real rain, that thing sits there full of leaves and nobody comes to clean it. I've mentioned it before and the leaves are still there.
I'm sorry, that's miserable. Is water getting into the house or the garage, or is it staying in the driveway?

Right now it's in the driveway and the street, up over the curb almost. But I'm worried about next door. My neighbor, Mr. Pacheco, he's older, he's in his eighties, and he can't get out. The water's across the bottom of his walk and he doesn't do well with steps. He's stuck in there.
Is he okay otherwise? Does he need emergency help, medical, anything like that?
No, no, he's fine, I just checked on him through the door. He's got his groceries. He just can't go anywhere. I don't want it to be an emergency, I want somebody to come clear the drain before it is.

Understood. I'm putting this in as a clogged catch basin with standing water at 175 Dixon Street, and I'm flagging that there's an elderly resident who's blocked in. Crews are stretched after the storm, so I can't give you a time, but it goes to the top of the list for the on-call crew.

Well, I appreciate that. I do. I just wish it didn't take a storm and a Sunday phone call. You know, I had to come across the bridge yesterday before it got bad, and the toll's gone up again. Again! They take a little more every time and the drains still don't get cleaned.
[pause] Yeah, I've heard that one from a few people. I can't do anything about the toll, but I can get this drain looked at.
No, I know, dear, it's not you. It just all adds up.
It does. Can I get a good number for you?
It's 401-555-0157. And would you have somebody call me back when it's done? Not before, I mean after they've cleared it. I'd like to know it's finished so I can tell Mr. Pacheco.
Yes, I'll note that, a callback once the crew has cleared it. 401-555-0157, right?
That's right. Thank you, honey. You have a good rest of your Sunday.
You too, Ms. Amaral. Stay out of that water.
